To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factor hypoxias‐inducible factors (HIF‐s) play a critical role in adaptation to hypoxic stress and that HIF‐s function is impaired in senescence.
the transcription factor HIF‐1 plays a critical role during the hypoxic stress response.
aging is associated with a decrease in the capacity of tissues to form a HRE complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hypoxia and HIF‐1 in aging and age‐associated diseases.
the role of HIF‐1 in the adaptation of tissues to hypoxic stress and the role of HRE in this process.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the decreased capacity of senescent organisms to respond to stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the function of HIF‐1 is impaired in senescence and this may contribute to the decreased capacity of senescent organisms to respond to hypoxia.
the function of HIF‐1 is impaired in senescence and that the impairment is not related to a reduction in the level of HIF‐α protein.
the function of HIF‐1 in senescent organisms is impaired.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIF‐1 system is impaired in senescence, and the HIF‐2α subunit of the HIF‐transcription factor is the most sensitive to aging.
aging is associated with a decrease in the capacity to produce HIF‐1, and that this decrease is associated with a decreased ability to respond to hypoxia.
aging impairs the capacity of tissues to respond to a variety of stresses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the aging process is accompanied by an attenuation in the capacity of cells to form HIF1‐HRE transcription factor complexes, and that this may explain, in part, the decreased ability of aged tissues to adapt to and recover from acute hypoxic insults.
aging is associated with impaired HIF‐1 function, a defect that may be responsible for the decreased capacity of senescent organisms to cope with hypoxia.
the function of the HIF‐1 pathway is impaired in senescence.
